messages:
joel-cust: Hey team — our EU dedicated pool (eu2-reserved-3) started returning sporadic 429s and p95 generation latency jumped from ~120ms to ~820ms around 08:12 UTC. No config changes on our side. Can you check?

nina-support: Sorry you're hitting this, Joel. Can you paste a couple of example request IDs or a short curl that reproduces? Any model/version pinned?

joel-cust: model: redwood/gpt-small@v2. Request IDs: r-0a3f2c, r-0a3f7d. curl example:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-small@v2","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":64}'
```

Responses look like: `HTTP/1.1 429 \n{\"error\":\"capacity_throttle\",\"code\":\"POOL_BUSY\"}`

liam-sre: Thanks. I'm pulling infra metrics now. Do you see throttles only for that pool or other dedicated pools? Also approximate qps/burst pattern?

joel-cust: Only eu2-reserved-3. Their app had a deploy yesterday that increased small-batch QPS (many concurrent 1-2 token responses). Peak ~45 qps sustained for 10m, with spikes to 120 qps for 30s.

liam-sre: That pattern (many tiny responses) can saturate SMs and preempt KV cache warmup. Initial checks: node packing shows mixed slice widths on affected hosts. running quick nvml/dmon snapshot: 

```
# nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT
# sample lines
08:11:50  3  99  0  2 124  0  1  0  1234
08:12:10  3  98  0  2 130  0  3  0  1600
```

SM util spikes to ~98% during bursts, L2 read throughput jumps, and pcie latency jitter observed. Not classic full-eviction, looks like co-hosted small-batch kernels saturating SMs on fractional MIG slices.

anika-infra: FYI we rolled a scheduler tweak yesterday that packs fractional MIG slices more aggressively to improve GPU utilization. Looks like on some 1g.5g slices the packing led to heterogeneous workloads collocated, which increases context switch overhead and causes transient throttles. I'm pulling node allocation logs now.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: [2026-03-12T08:10:30Z] scaled pool eu2-reserved-3 +2 slots (packing_policy=aggressive_fractional)

liam-sre: That matches timeline. We should isolate whether it's packing vs KV cache eviction. Quick repro steps for support (what I'll run):
1) attach to one affected host: `ssh infra@host-eu2-07`
2) `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep eu2-reserved-3`
3) run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv -l 1` and `nv-hostengine` traces for 60s during traffic spike
4) capture scheduler allocation log: `/var/log/redwood/scheduler/alloc.log` for 08:05-08:20 UTC

liam-sre: Preliminary root-cause hypothesis: aggressive fractional packing + bursty tiny responses -> SM oversubscription on MIG slices -> increased kernel preemption & PCIe stalls -> scheduler returns capacity_throttle to callers as protective measure.

nina-support: Joel — we can apply a quick mitigator while infra triages: 1) throttle client QPS (burst limiter) to reduce concurrent tiny requests, or 2) pin your workloads to 2g.10g slices (if you have entitlement) to avoid fractional slices. Which option is easier for you?

joel-cust: We can add client-side limiter quickly. Can you also repro so we can know if bumping slice helps long-term?

anika-infra: I'll repro on a canary host with a synthetic workload that mimics your small-batch QPS and attach perf counters. If we see SM tail latency spikes and frequent kernel preemption, we'll revert the aggressive_fractional packing flag for eu2 region.

liam-sre: For the internal ticket I'll collect: sched logs, node nvml traces, `dmesg | tail -n 200`, and per-tenant throttles from the control plane for 07:55-08:30 UTC. Also check: any MIG reconfigs around that time? (MIG is static but we log reassignments).

joel-cust: Thanks. I'll roll the client limiter now and report back in 15m.

nina-support: Noted. Status: mitigation applied by customer (client limiter). We'll monitor. I'll update the ticket with liam/anika outputs. :thumbsup:

anika-infra: Update 08:45 UTC — reproduced on canary with synthetic 1-2 token bursts. Observed: SM busy ~96-99% and NVML shows kernel preempt events ~120/sec on 1g.5g slices. Reverting packing_policy to conservative for eu2-reserved-3 stops the 429s in our replay. Plan: rollback packing policy for affected pools + schedule a controlled re-eval of packing heuristic.

liam-sre: Good. Action items:
- anika: rollback packing_policy (in progress)
- nina: coordinate customer notification and recommend longer-term: either pin to larger slices or shape traffic into slightly larger batches
- joel: confirm whether limiter reduced 429s

joel-cust: Limiter cut 429s to 0 within 5m and p95 back to ~140ms. Thanks all.

nina-support: Closing loop: we'll keep eu2-reserved-3 on conservative packing for 24h and then run controlled experiments. I'll add postmortem notes and link metrics in the ticket.

liam-sre: Adding quick log excerpt for the ticket:
```
[08:12:11] capacity_throttle: pool=eu2-reserved-3 tenant=joel-corp requests=120 qps=85 sm_util=98 preempt_events=118
```

nina-support: Thanks team — putting this in P1 follow-up.

deploy-bot: incident-note: [2026-03-12] eu2 fractional-packing rollback initiated by anika-infra
